subject: .skills/fleet-explain-component
verdict: Lean, well-structured one-shot utility with strong script/prompt separation; the primary gap is no headless mode for batch automation and no graceful degradation when dependencies are absent.
summary: The skill is impressively lean at 1212 tokens with clear outcome-driven structure and excellent delegation of deterministic parsing to shared scripts. Its primary weakness is that it was built interactive-only — no headless path for batch readme generation across all components, no fallback when web search or scripts are unavailable, and repo-specific product mappings hardcoded rather than externalized.

themes.title: No automation path
themes.root_cause: The skill was built interactive-only without considering that batch readme generation across all 52 components is a natural use case for one of five fleet workflows sharing common scripts.
themes.action: Add three-mode architecture: Guided (current), Yolo (auto-approve readme writes), Headless (suppress chat, emit structured output, exit). Make readme generation opt-in in guided mode, automatic in yolo/headless.

themes.title: Hardcoded repo-specific data without customization surface
themes.root_cause: Product mappings, template path, and web-search behavior are baked into the skill body. This forces a fork for any repo that uses a different readme format, has different component-to-product mappings, or operates in an air-gapped environment.
themes.action: Add a customize.toml with: product_mappings path (externalize the 5-entry table to a CSV/JSON data file), readme_template path, web_search boolean default true. SKILL.md reads these as {workflow.<name>}.

themes.title: No graceful degradation
themes.root_cause: Every dependency (Python scripts, web search, fleet-common references) is treated as mandatory with no fallback. A hostile environment (air-gapped, missing fleet-common, script error) produces unhandled failures.
themes.action: Add a Graceful degradation clause: script failures fall back to manual file listing; web search failures fall back to manifest-only analysis with a 'locally-derived' marker; missing references proceed without architectural context and note the gap.

themes.title: Structural compliance nits
themes.root_cause: Minor heading-level violation and an unused resolution-rule entry from the build process.
themes.action: Change `# Overview` to `## Overview`, remove unused `{skill-root}` resolution rule, unnumber step 4 (fleet-repo-structure.md load is order-independent).

strengths: Excellent script/prompt boundary — all deterministic parsing delegated to shared Python scripts that return structured JSON
Lean at 1212 tokens (well under 1500 desired budget) with no waste patterns or back-references
Institutional knowledge (Gotchas section) captures the non-derivable repo-specific edge cases a bare model would miss
Domain-specific Mermaid examples calibrate diagram output for this repo's relationship types
Outcome-driven structure — tells the model what to produce, not a step-by-step march

recommendations.action: Add three-mode architecture (guided/yolo/headless) with structured output in headless mode
Add customize.toml with product_mappings, readme_template, and web_search scalars; externalize product mappings to a data file
Add graceful degradation for each dependency (scripts, web search, references)
Fix heading level (# → ##), remove unused {skill-root}, unnumber step 4
Add a list_component_resources.py script to fleet-common that enumerates manifests and extracts resource metadata as JSON

journeys.name: Expert with clear intent
journeys.steps: Invokes with component name → gets full explanation + readme proposal → approves or declines. Works well.

journeys.name: First-timer
journeys.steps: Invokes → gets dense technical output with repo-specific terminology and no orientation. Workable but could be smoother.

journeys.name: Automator (batch)
journeys.steps: Cannot invoke headless. Blocked entirely by approval gate and chat-only output.

journeys.name: Air-gapped environment
journeys.steps: Web search fails with no fallback. Partial explanation produced but product identification is weak.

experience.headless: Not supported. Adding headless mode is the single highest-leverage enhancement given the batch-orchestration context.

findings.title: No headless mode — blocks automation entirely
findings.evidence: The skill mandates 'ask for approval before writing' with no way to bypass it. An automator wanting to batch-generate readmes for all components hits a blocking prompt on every invocation. There is no --headless or --auto-approve path, and no structured output contract.
findings.recommendation: Add Three-mode architecture. Guided (current behavior), Yolo (skip approval, write readme directly), Headless (suppress chat explanation, emit only the readme as a structured artifact to a known path, exit zero/non-zero).

findings.title: No graceful degradation for dependency failures
findings.evidence: Step 1 handles 'component not found' but nothing else. If Python isn't available, if find_component_siblings.py has a runtime error, if fleet-common/references/fleet-repo-structure.md is missing, or if the web search returns nothing, the skill has no fallback path.
findings.recommendation: Add a Graceful degradation section. For each dependency name the fallback: script failures → manual directory listing; missing references → proceed without; web search failure → manifest-only analysis marked as 'locally-derived'.

findings.title: No intent-before-ingestion — wrong-intent user gets a wall of output
findings.evidence: The skill goes from activation straight to running scripts, reading all YAML manifests, and web-searching before producing any output. A user who says 'what does metallb do' wanting a two-sentence answer gets a multi-section explanation with Mermaid diagrams and a readme proposal.
findings.recommendation: Add a single soft gate after resolving the lifecycle group: 'Found <N> parts in the <name> lifecycle group. I'll produce a full explanation with diagrams and a readme. Want the full treatment, or just a quick summary?'

findings.title: Overview uses h1 instead of h2
findings.evidence: Skill begins with `# Overview` (h1). Pre-pass flagged 'Missing ## Overview section'. In BMad skill structure the frontmatter name serves as the implicit h1; body sections must start at h2.
findings.recommendation: Change `# Overview` to `## Overview`.

findings.title: Product-mapping table hardcoded in skill body
findings.evidence: Five component-to-product mappings are embedded as prose in the skill. Every new component requires editing SKILL.md itself.
findings.recommendation: Extract mappings to a data file (CSV or JSON) referenced via customize.toml. The skill reads the file at runtime; repos extend it without touching the skill.

findings.title: No plan-validate-execute — user can't course-correct before heavy work
findings.evidence: The skill reads all YAML manifests, loads architectural context, does web searches, generates diagrams, and generates a readme — all before the user sees anything. If the sibling resolution pulled in the wrong group, all that work is wasted.
findings.recommendation: After step 2, emit a brief plan showing the resolved group and intended outputs. One confirmation before the expensive steps.

findings.title: Dual-output is unconditional — readme generation is forced
findings.evidence: The Readme Generation section always fires. An expert who just wants to understand a component before debugging doesn't want a readme proposal.
findings.recommendation: Make readme generation opt-in in guided mode. After the explanation, ask: 'Want me to generate/update the readme?' In headless mode, always generate.

findings.title: Web search is mandated with no offline fallback
findings.evidence: 'Web-search for the upstream project documentation' is an imperative with no fallback. In a disconnected environment the skill stalls or produces an error.
findings.recommendation: Reframe as best-effort: 'Web-search if available. If unavailable, use known-mappings and manifest analysis. Mark product identification as locally-derived when web sources weren't consulted.'

findings.title: Readme template path hardcoded
findings.evidence: Template fixed to `{fleet-common}/references/readme-template.md`. A repo wanting a different format must fork.
findings.recommendation: Add customize.toml [paths].readme_template defaulting to the current path.

findings.title: No on_complete hook after readme write
findings.evidence: After readme is written, no mechanism to chain follow-up actions (lint, git stage, update index).
findings.recommendation: Add customize.toml [hooks].on_complete supporting a post-write action.

findings.title: Web-search behavior not toggleable
findings.evidence: Unconditional web search. Air-gapped or policy-restricted environments fail.
findings.recommendation: Add customize.toml [workflow].web_search = true (default). When false, skip search and rely on manifest analysis and product-mapping data file.

findings.title: Prompt enumerates and parses YAML manifests
findings.evidence: Step 3 instructs the prompt to 'Read all YAML manifests in each part directory' and 'Understand what Kubernetes resources are created.' Enumerating files and extracting resource kind/apiVersion/name is deterministic plumbing.
findings.recommendation: Add a list_component_resources.py script that walks part dirs, parses YAML, and returns JSON [{file, kind, apiVersion, name, namespace, annotations}]. The prompt interprets meaning; the script handles fetch-and-parse.

findings.title: Sequence diagram example is calibration weight without proportional return
findings.evidence: Two full Mermaid examples (~150 tokens). The architecture diagram concretely calibrates the expected style. The sequence diagram demonstrates a standard Mermaid pattern models produce correctly without demonstration.
findings.recommendation: Cut the sequence diagram example. Keep the architecture diagram example and append: 'Also generate a sequence diagram when multi-part sync-wave ordering is non-obvious.'

findings.title: Product Identification sources bullets teach what model would naturally do
findings.evidence: First two bullets describe inference steps a capable model would take automatically after reading operator-policy.yaml.
findings.recommendation: Collapse into lead-in: 'Map the component to its upstream project using OperatorPolicy metadata and these repo-specific mappings:'

findings.title: Component Description first bullet fails core test
findings.evidence: 'What the product/project does (from upstream docs, 2-3 sentences)' instructs what a model asked to 'explain a component' would do without prompting.
findings.recommendation: Remove the bullet. The product description is implied by the overall instruction.

findings.title: Gotcha duplicates AGENTS.md workspace rule
findings.evidence: The gitops-boostrap-policy typo gotcha is identical to the always-applied workspace rule in AGENTS.md.
findings.recommendation: Delete the bullet. The workspace rule covers it unconditionally.

findings.title: On Activation step 4 is not sequentially dependent
findings.evidence: Step 4 ('Load fleet-repo-structure.md') has no dependency on steps 1-3. Placing it in a numbered sequence implies a dependency that doesn't exist.
findings.recommendation: Move to Overview or a context note. Reserve numbering for truly ordered steps 1-3.

findings.title: Unused resolution-rule entry {skill-root}
findings.evidence: `{skill-root}` is defined but never referenced anywhere in the skill body.
findings.recommendation: Remove or add a reference that uses it.

findings.title: Hardcoded product-mapping lookup table in prompt
findings.evidence: Five key→value mappings embedded as prose. This is a deterministic lookup that should be a data file.
findings.recommendation: Move to a data file (fleet-common/references/product-mappings.json). Have the skill load it at runtime.

findings.title: Readme existence re-checked when script already returns it
findings.evidence: find_component_siblings.py already returns readme_path. The Readme Generation section tells the prompt to 'check if the component has a readme.md' — repeating a deterministic check the script already performed.
findings.recommendation: Reword to reference the script output: 'Using the readme_path from the siblings output, determine whether a readme exists.'

findings.title: Approval gate not bypassable for automation
findings.evidence: Mandates 'ask for approval before writing.' In headless or batch-mode invocations, blocks on interactive confirmation.
findings.recommendation: Add customize.toml [workflow].auto_approve = false (default). When true, write readme immediately.

findings.title: No open-floor orientation for first-timers
findings.evidence: First-timer receives dense technical explanation using repo-specific terminology (lifecycle groups, sync-waves) without introduction.
findings.recommendation: Add a brief orientation block at the start of Explanation output: 'This repo organizes components into lifecycle groups...'

findings.title: Capture-don't-interrupt opportunity missed
findings.evidence: During manifest analysis, the skill may encounter anomalies (missing CRDs, uncommented blocks, namespace mismatches). Currently no mechanism to capture and present these separately from the main explanation.
findings.recommendation: Add an 'observations' capture: anomalies collected during analysis get presented in a separate section after the explanation rather than interrupting the narrative.
